sections.title: Saying where something is
sections.content: Hungarian has no separate word for “in”. It adds an ending to the noun: *-ban* or *-ben*. Which one depends on the vowels in the word. A word with a back vowel (*a, á, o, ó, u, ú*) takes *-ban*. A word with only front vowels (*e, é, ö, ő, ü, ű*) takes *-ben*. The vowels *i* and *í* are neutral: they go along with the other vowels in the word.

sections.title: The long vowel
sections.content: When a word ends in *-a* or *-e*, that last vowel grows long as the ending is added: *szoba* becomes *szobában*, with *á*. *Fürdőszoba* and *hálószoba* are compounds, and their last part, *szoba*, decides: they take *-ban* too.

items.english: The book is in the bathroom.

sections.content: English puts “in” before the noun. Hungarian puts the ending after it, and the article *a* stays in front: *a szobában*. Say the word, add the ending and keep the accent: *szobában* is right, *szobaban* is not. *A* and *á* are different letters.
